record.paper_title: Open Problems in Heavy Quarkonium Physics
record.original_question: Are the approximately equal radial spacings seen in the low-lying bottomonium spectrum merely a numerical coincidence of perturbative calculations with leading-order renormalon cancellation, or do they genuinely reflect that these states are Coulombic or quasi-Coulombic bound states? Resolving this requires further theoretical and phenomenological study of higher bottomonium levels and their fine splittings.

evidence.quote: If this is coincidental or reflects the (quasi-)Coulombic nature of the states will be decided by further studies.

It seems to indicate either the existence of large NLL/NNLO corrections (as it happens in the hyperfine splittings of the 1S levels) or sizeable non-perturbative corrections, somehow hidden in the error bands of Fig. 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the framework of non-relativistic QCD applied to heavy quarkonium, consider the low-lying bottomonium spectrum (the b\bar b bound states such as the Υ(nS) family for n=1,2,3, together with their χ_b and η_b partners). Empirically, the radial level spacings between successive S-wave states are observed to be approximately equal. In perturbative computations of the static QCD potential, the leading u=1/2 infrared renormalon of the potential cancels against the renormalon of twice the heavy-quark pole mass when one expresses the pole mass in terms of a short-distance mass (e.g. the MS-bar, PS, or MSR mass); after this leading-order renormalon cancellation, the perturbative predictions for radial spacings come out close to the observed values.

Determine whether this near-equality of radial spacings in bottomonium is:
(a) merely a numerical coincidence arising from perturbative calculations after leading-order renormalon cancellation (potentially due to large NLL/NNLO corrections analogous to those in 1S hyperfine splittings, or to sizeable non-perturbative corrections hidden within current error bands), or
(b) a genuine reflection of the fact that these bottomonium states are Coulombic or quasi-Coulombic bound states (i.e. dominated by the perturbative one-gluon-exchange Coulomb-like interaction, with non-perturbative contributions subleading).

Provide a theoretical and phenomenological resolution by analysing higher bottomonium levels and their fine splittings in a manner that decisively distinguishes (a) from (b).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent N3LO NRQCD analyses of the bottomonium spectrum (e.g. global fits at N3LO around 2018, and N3LO bottom-mass extractions) report that n=1,2 bottomonium levels are well described perturbatively after renormalon cancellation, while n=3 states show poor perturbative convergence, leaving the Coulombic-versus-coincidence interpretation of the regular radial spacings unresolved. No conclusive demonstration favoring (a) or (b) has appeared, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Bottom and charm mass determinations from global fits to QQ̄ bound states at N3LO
status_evidence.snippet: Bottomonium spectrum up to n=3 studied within NRQCD at N3LO; n=1,2 well behaved in perturbation theory while n=3 bound states are no longer reliable.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art perturbative analyses still cannot reliably reach higher bottomonium radial excitations, so the (quasi-)Coulombic interpretation of equal radial spacings is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Perturbative QCD Potential, Renormalon Cancellation and Phenomenological Potentials
status_evidence.snippet: After renormalon cancellation, the total energy agrees well with phenomenological potentials at intermediate distances relevant to bottomonium.
status_evidence.claim: Renormalon-cancelled perturbative potential reproduces phenomenological behavior, but does not by itself decide whether equal radial spacings are coincidence or reflect Coulombic dynamics.
